gist: Art.8 cont.: modifications at Impresa's cost; 50 centesimi per sheet spoiled; cuts to be marked lightly in red pencil. Art.9: no copying, penalty £(lire) 6000; Lucca may station a trusted person to retrieve parts after each rehearsal/performance.
why: contract clauses

gist: Overlaps p.13; art.9 cont.: Lucca family/staff free entry to all rehearsals and performances. Art.10: any changes/additions/new pieces made by the composer or another maestro become Lucca's property without compensation.
why: contract clauses; partial overlap

gist: Art.11: librettos not to be printed locally; to be bought only from Ditta Lucca at «35%» (handwritten). Art.12-13: other customs void; Lucca may suspend performances on breach. Art.14 begins: opera to be given complete.

gist: Overlaps p.15; art.14: cuts need Lucca's written permission. Art.15: disputes to Milan tribunals. Signed «G. Lucca».
why: signature page of Lucca contract

from_to: Choudens père et fils -> Direction Impériale pour l'Opéra Italien à St-Pétersbourg

gist: French letter (no. 15, stamped paper): following your request I have sent the librettos of «Lalla Roukh» and «Le Domino noir»; as you wish to receive the music of Lalla as soon as possible, please answer... my letters have gone unanswered; the price is accepted but I asked who would sign the contract binding the music to be used only at the Russian theatre. Partly covered by an adjacent French contract between [Vsevol]ojsky, directeur des théâtres impériaux de Pétersbourg, and a music publisher at 2 rue Scribe for the opera «Néron» (words by M. Jules [Barbier?]), for the Italian Opera at St Petersburg.
why: Opera material correspondence; Néron contract glimpsed; no ballet

gist: Second photo of the p.43 letter (Lalla Roukh / Domino noir librettos), showing slightly more of the covered «Néron» contract: rights for the opera «Néron» for the Imperial Italian Opera at St Petersburg, signed by the Direction Impériale.
why: Duplicate view of p.43

gist: Continuation of the p.43 letter: only once the contract is in hand will the music be sent; such business is always done cash, so who pays and when? Writer cannot supply recitatives, any more than Brandus for «Le Domino», since Lalla and the Domino were performed and published as opéras comiques without recitatives; since M. Vizentini? has promised them for 300 fr., take them from him. Meanwhile the choruses are being sent under separate cover with the contract.
why: Recitatives for opéra comique at the Russian stage; no ballet

gist: End of Girod's letter (no. 16): asks that the contract be returned signed so she can send the music sooner; hopes there will be no further misunderstanding; will enclose the mise en scène with the music, at 12 fr. extra; signed Vve E. Girod. The «Néron» contract (p.47) again visible alongside.
why: Opera material correspondence (mise en scène for 12 fr.); no ballet

doc_type: contract (hire of music with performing rights)
from_to: E. Gérard, éditeur de musique (Paris, 2 rue Scribe) -> Son Excellence M. Jean Wsévolojsky, directeur des Théâtres Impériaux
gist: French contract on stamped paper (No. 8734; margin 1523, 1883; Russian «Утверждаю» at top): between I. A. Vsevolozhsky, director of the Imperial [Italian] Theatres of Petersburg and Moscow, and E. Gérard, exclusive owner (except Germany) of the opera «Néron», music by A. Rubinstein, words by Jules Barbier, Italian translation by de Lauzières. I: Gérard hires to the Direction for the 1883-84 season only the complete music of Néron, Italian edition, with performing rights on the two Italian stages of Petersburg and Moscow. Continues p.48.
why: Opera hire contract (Rubinstein's Néron); no ballet

gist: Overlaps p.47 and continues: II. material delivered marked 'Location' comprises the orchestral score of «Néron» with Italian words, complete orchestral parts plus 5 first violins, 4 second violins, 3 altos, 4 cellos and 5 double basses extra, vocal scores with Italian words for role study, and five [Italian scores for stage management...]. Pencil calculations in left margin.
why: Opera hire material list; no ballet

gist: «Néron» contract continued: five Italian scores for stage management, prompter etc., 90 chorus parts, three Italian manuscripts of Néron; all to be returned franco to Gérard when the 1883-84 Italian season ends. III. hire price for the season, with performing rights, four thousand francs, payable 2,000 fr. on 1 September and 2,000 fr. on 1 October 1883 (new style). IV. delivery in instalments. V. music for the sole use of the Italian theatres of Petersburg and Moscow, 1883-84, may not leave their library; Gérard may verify its presence.
why: Opera hire fee 4,000 fr.; no ballet

gist: End of the «Néron» contract (overlaps p.49): fee 4,000 fr. in two instalments of 2,000 fr. (1 Sept. and 1 Oct. 1883 n.s.); music may not leave the theatres' library; the Direction undertakes not to make or allow any partial or total copy. 'Fait double et de bonne foi à Paris 25 Mai 18[83]'; signed 'Approuvé E. Gérard'.
why: Opera hire fee and copying ban; no ballet
